title: HDFC Bank Weighs Deputy MD Bharucha and External Candidate for CEO Succession
excerpt: India's largest private lender is fast-tracking its leadership search after CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan announced he will not seek reappointment when his term ends in October.
body:
• HDFC Bank is likely to name Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha as one of two candidates for the CEO position, according to Reuters, citing people familiar with the matter.
  • The bank is also searching for an external candidate, as RBI rules require banks to submit multiple names for CEO appointments.
  • CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan announced Saturday he will not seek reappointment after his second term ends in October, following months of governance upheaval.
  • HDFC Bank shares have fallen 27% this year, with the decline accelerating after former chairman Atanu Chakraborty's resignation in March.

HDFC Bank, India's largest private sector lender, is weighing Deputy Managing Director Kaizad Bharucha and an external candidate as its top options for the next chief executive, according to two people familiar with the matter cited by Reuters. The search follows incumbent CEO Sashidhar Jagdishan's announcement Saturday that he will not seek a third term.

Bharucha Emerges as Internal Frontrunner

Bharucha, a long-serving executive who oversees HDFC Bank's retail and wholesale banking businesses, has emerged as the leading internal candidate. He was among those considered for the CEO role in 2020 when Jagdishan was selected to succeed founding CEO Aditya Puri, according to the Times of India.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=Kn7PZu8Rl1M

Bharucha is not due to retire until 2029, when he will have completed 15 years as a full-time director — the maximum tenure permitted under Reserve Bank of India rules, though exemptions can be sought. His longevity at the bank and his elevation to executive director rank position him as a continuity candidate at a time of significant institutional flux.

External Names in the Mix

The RBI requires banks to submit multiple names when seeking approval for CEO appointments. Industry observers have flagged K. Balasubramanian, CEO of Citi India and a former head of corporate banking at HDFC Bank, and Hitendra Dave, CEO of HSBC India, as potential external candidates, according to the Times of India.

An external appointment would mark a departure from HDFC Bank's tradition of promoting from within — a practice that defined the Puri era and continued with Jagdishan's appointment.

Six Months of Upheaval

The CEO search caps a turbulent period for the bank. Former chairman Atanu Chakraborty resigned in March, citing practices at odds with his "personal values and ethics." An external legal review subsequently found no evidence to support Chakraborty's governance concerns, according to Reuters.

Last month, the board penalized Jagdishan and three other executives over the pricing of large institutional deposits. The cumulative effect has weighed on the bank's stock, which has fallen 27% in 2026 — with the decline accelerating after Chakraborty's departure.

"Kaizad is a very dear colleague, and I have the highest regard and respect for him. He will only get more responsibilities as we move forward."

— Sashidhar Jagdishan, HDFC Bank CEO, on an earlier analyst call

Merger Overhang Persists

Investor sentiment has also been shaped by the aftermath of HDFC Bank's $40 billion merger with parent HDFC Ltd in 2023. The deal added Rs 7.23 trillion in assets but brought a relatively small deposit base, squeezing margins and dragging on growth. The bank's net interest margin has dipped to 3.35% from 4.1% pre-merger, and it has had to slow asset growth to stabilize its loan-to-deposit ratio, which rose to around 110% from 86-87% before the merger.

What's Next

HDFC Bank said it will fast-track the appointment of a successor. The RBI must approve the final selection. Sources told Reuters a new CEO is expected to be in place before Jagdishan steps down in October. HDFC Bank shares, roughly 40% foreign-owned as of June, will be closely watched for market reaction when trading resumes.
